summary: Re-ran test_iter55_hardcap_prompts.py (-n 0) against live backend with round-3 prompt fixes (5 fields restructured to single-sentence 15-word cap / lowered how_to_start to 9w / weekly_plan.summary to 10w), using a THIRD fresh custom career 'Specjalista ds. marketingu cyfrowego' to bypass cache. Updated test's hardcoded career title + printed TARGET annotations for the 5 changed fields. All 5 test functions PASSED (assertions are intentionally loose; real signal is printed word counts), 0 JSON parse failures across ~7 live AI calls, ~48s runtime. All 7 previously-compliant field types (steps, free_tips, weekly tips, task/milestone description for 8/9 sampled items, daily plan) remain compliant. The 5 target fields still exceed their NEW lower caps: recommendations.summary 25w/cap15, career_detail.description 24w/cap15 (and observed as 2 sentences, not the required single sentence), career_detail.how_to_start 10-17w/cap9 (worse ratio than iter55 since cap dropped from 11 to 9), task_resources.overview 22w/cap15, weekly_plan.summary 13w/cap10. Structural counts unchanged and correct: 8 weeks, 6 named resources, 6 how_to_start items, 3 milestones x 3 tasks.

minor.issue: Cap=15 words (1 sentence); observed 25 words. Improved in absolute terms from iter55 (32w) but overshoot % is similar/slightly worse relative to new lower cap (+67% vs cap).

Cap=15 words/1 sentence; observed 24 words AND rendered as 2 sentences, same as iteration_55's 2-sentence version despite the prompt now explicitly asking for '1 zwięzłe zdanie'. Model is not following the single-sentence restructure for this field.

Cap lowered 11->9 words/item; observed 10,14,13,10,16,17 words (6 items), essentially unchanged from iteration_55's 10,14,13,10,16,16 — lowering the cap had almost no effect on output length, so overshoot % increased from the stricter cap.
Cap=15 words/1 sentence; observed 22 words (single sentence, correctly structured). Improved from iter55's 26w but still 47% over cap.
Cap lowered 12->10 words; observed 13 words (single sentence). Small, consistent overshoot, same as prior rounds.

action_items: Per agent-to-agent context note: this is flagged as the final calibration round and 1-3 word overshoots should not be chased further. However, 3 of the 5 fields overshoot by MORE than 1-3 words even after lowering caps (recommendations.summary +10w, career_detail.description +9w AND still 2 sentences not 1, how_to_start +1 to +8w per item) — these are not minor 1-3w misses, they are the same magnitude of overshoot as iteration_55, just measured against a lower cap. Lowering the stated cap further did not meaningfully shorten the actual model output for these 3 fields.

career_detail.description specifically did not adopt the '1 sentence' instruction at all (still outputs 2 sentences, identical word count to iteration_55's 2-sentence version) — this suggests the model may be ignoring/not seeing the updated single-sentence instruction, or FAST_MODEL caching/determinism is producing near-identical output regardless of the sentence-count instruction change. Worth a quick sanity check that the prompt string at line ~1033 is actually being sent (no stale import/caching) if further iteration is desired.

task_resources.overview and weekly_plan.summary DID correctly adopt single-sentence structure and showed real improvement (26w->22w, 14w->13w), consistent with the pattern that fields without a competing 'name real courses/platforms' requirement respond well to cap tightening.

Given the explicit instruction in this task not to keep chasing further micro-overshoots and that output quality/coherence is good, recommend treating this as the final state for this calibration task UNLESS product owner requires hard enforcement — in which case the only path left is programmatic post-processing (truncate/regenerate) rather than more prompt wording changes, since 3 rounds of prompt tightening have not closed the gap for the 'concrete-naming' fields.
critical_code_review_comments: 0 JSON parse failures / truncations across 7 live AI calls in this run — ask_llm() parsing remains robust.

Verified in server.py: recommendations.summary prompt (line ~936) and career_detail.description prompt (line ~1033) both now correctly say '1 zwięzłe zdanie, maks. 15 słów' as intended by the round-3 fix; the overshoot is a model-compliance issue, not a prompt-authoring bug.
No structural regressions: 8 weeks in study plan, 6 resources, 6 how_to_start items, 3 milestones each with 3 tasks.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_iter55_hardcap_prompts.py (career title + TARGET annotations updated for retest only, no behavior change)

success_rate.backend: 100% (5/5 tests passed, loose assertions; 0/7 live AI calls had JSON parse failures)

seed_data_creation: Fresh TEST_iter55_* user (new uuid), premium demo subscription, profile answers, recommendations, custom career 'Specjalista ds. marketingu cyfrowego' (new title, bypasses career_templates cache), roadmap, task resources, 8-week study plan, daily plan settings.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Round-3 targeted fixes (single-sentence restructure + lower caps for 5 fields) show mixed results: task_resources.overview and weekly_plan.summary improved meaningfully; recommendations.summary and career_detail.how_to_start barely changed in absolute word count despite lower caps (so overshoot % got worse); career_detail.description still outputs 2 sentences despite the prompt now asking for exactly 1. Per the task's own instructions, further micro-chasing of 1-3 word overshoots is NOT warranted, and all output remains coherent, grammatical, complete Polish sentences conveying real substantive content (no truncation/garbling observed anywhere). This can reasonably be considered the final acceptable calibration state unless exact hard-cap enforcement becomes a strict product requirement, at which point programmatic truncation (not further prompt tuning) is the recommended next step.
rca_of_issue: Consistent with iterations 54-55's RCA: fields requiring BOTH a tight word cap AND naming concrete real-world entities (courses, platforms, universities) within the same sentence structurally compete, and the LLM prioritizes concreteness over the word cap. Lowering the stated cap further (e.g. how_to_start 11->9) did not proportionally shorten the actual output — the model appears to have a soft 'floor' around 10-17 words for a how_to_start item that names a concrete course/platform/institution, largely independent of the stated max. Likewise career_detail.description's 2-sentence structure appears resistant to the 'single sentence' instruction, possibly because describing BOTH 'what the job does' and 'what a typical day looks like' (both still requested in the surrounding prompt context) naturally invites 2 clauses/sentences regardless of the explicit count instruction.
